label: A0
title: How to approach a design question
scope: Planning arithmetic, hand-authored SLI classification and a real SQLite repository probe. No HTTP service, authentication implementation, hosted resources, model/provider calls or production benchmark.

label: A1
title: Application architecture and service boundaries
scope: Loopback Express HTTP, fixed public lesson-token allowlist, real file-backed synchronous SQLite, direct service calls and AST dependency checks. Parallel requests run in one Node process; no distributed concurrency, OAuth/TLS, durable events, proxies, production capacity or microservices deployment verified.

label: A2
title: Data, caching and scaling
scope: Real local SQLite index plans, VM instruction counts, scoped keyset queries and conditional writes. Deterministic asyncio interleavings over process-local caches and two SQLite connections. TTL uses an injected clock; scaling/placement are hypothetical arithmetic. No Redis, HTTP/authentication, replicated database, sharded deployment, network partition or production throughput verified.

label: A3
title: Reliable workflows and concurrency
scope: Real SQLite operation replay, atomic note/outbox creation, separate consumer inbox/effect transactions, close/reopen recovery, lease generations, attempt bounds, two-connection races and idempotent local compensation. Retry transport/time and lease time are injected; crash boundaries omit steps or raise controlled exceptions. No process-kill/power-loss, broker/provider/network, PostgreSQL isolation, distributed lease target, full saga coordinator or production throughput verified.

label: A4
title: Operating a secure and observable system
scope: Real loopback HTTP authorization with published lesson tokens, current SQLite membership/scoped reads, two-connection atomic fixed-window quotas, private text-upload quarantine, application readiness/drain/admission and bounded diagnostic records. Dependency failure and held work are controlled flags/barriers. SLI samples and capacity/cost inputs are authored offline exercises. No production authentication/TLS, antivirus/object storage, Kubernetes/signal rollout, OTel/Prometheus backend, production SLO or throughput capacity verified.

label: S0
title: URL shortener
scope: Real local SQLite allocation/replay/rollback and two-connection collision/duplicate races; real loopback HTTP create/manage/GET/HEAD redirect/expiry/disable/stats without following destinations. Process-local bounded cache, injected expiry clock and explicitly lossy in-memory analytics with durable bounded-age aggregates. Estimates are hypothetical. No production auth/TLS, unrestricted destination validation, Redis/CDN, durable analytics delivery, multi-host cache coherence, PostgreSQL isolation or throughput capacity verified.

label: S1
title: Rate limiter
scope: Local Python/SQLite and loopback HTTP. No Redis, production authentication/TLS, distributed clock authority, multi-region failover or capacity benchmark. Denials do not charge tokens; successful admissions charge even if work fails. Fail-open intentionally relaxes enforcement.

label: S2
title: Notification and webhook delivery service
scope: Local Python/SQLite durable queue plus owned signed loopback HTTP receiver. No external messages, SMTP/SMS/push integration, vendor account, broker, production authentication/TLS, crash-power-loss, distributed clock/failover or load benchmark. At-least-once attempts are bounded; receiver effect dedupe is a local transactional record, not universal exactly-once delivery.

label: S3
title: File upload, storage and processing service
scope: Owned local files/SQLite and actual loopback HTTP only. Immutable 1 KiB text objects, custom bearer capability and deterministic content policy; no S3 emulation, multipart transfer, antivirus, general document safety, external uploads, production authentication/TLS, distributed locking/clock, power-loss guarantee or load benchmark. Local writes and inventory cleanup share the SQLite write authority; cloud direct uploads require a different coordination protocol.

label: S4
title: Ticket booking and limited-inventory reservation
scope: Local SQLite assigned-seat authority and signed loopback callback only. No real payment/refund, provider SDK, distributed clock/lock, PostgreSQL execution, production auth/TLS or load benchmark. Refund rows are durable pending intents, not executed refunds.

label: S5
title: Chat and real-time messaging
scope: Local SQLite room history and bounded process-local hints with actual loopback HTTP polling. No WebSocket/SSE protocol, external messages, Redis/broker, production auth/TLS, distributed sequencing/clock, load test or proof of human reading. Current members can read retained history; removed members cannot use new API requests.

label: S6
title: Social feed and photo sharing
scope: Bounded local SQLite hybrid chronological feed and actual loopback JSON HTTP. Media state is a trusted metadata fixture, not image decoding, S3 integration or signed image delivery. No recommendation/ranking engine, production auth/TLS, distributed fanout/cache, global revocation or load benchmark. Visibility is rechecked for each local request; already delivered pages cannot be retracted.

label: S7
title: Background job scheduler and worker platform
scope: Local SQLite scheduling, coalesced interval occurrences, two-slot tenant admission, fenced leases, local transactional effect dedupe, bounded retries, rollback and actual loopback HTTP. Explicit time inputs; no cron daemon, broker, external effect or production load test.

label: S8
title: Checkout, payments and credit ledger
scope: Separate local provider and merchant SQLite stores; injected reply loss after provider commit, immutable catalog snapshots, signed fixture callback, payment/event/grant dedupe, balanced integer credit journals, competing spends, reversal, rollback and real merchant loopback HTTP. No real charge, bank ledger, card data, refund or provider network.

label: S9
title: Search and autocomplete
scope: Actual SQLite FTS5 full text and title-token prefix search; canonical ACL, tenant and version checks before top-k results, versioned outbox, stale/tombstone fences, rollback, two projector calls, local atomic rebuild and real HTTP. Selected relevance judgements only; no external search cluster, semantic ranking, online reindex or performance benchmark.

label: S10
title: Load balancer and distributed cache
scope: Deterministic placement sample, in-process least-active routing/drain labels, bounded copied LRU caches, guarded fill/version/delete/epoch checks, controlled failure/rejoin, four competing calls, SQLite rollback/reopen and actual edge HTTP. No network proxy, distributed membership, Redis replication, automatic detector, quorum or throughput benchmark.

label: S11
title: Multi-tenant SaaS with authentication and permissions
scope: Local durable hashed opaque bearer sessions after trusted fixture login, current membership/role and tenant/document/share checks, rotated tenant switch, expiring revocable recipient/audience-bound invitation capabilities, atomic quota and audit, scoped metadata export with worker/delivery rechecks, four competing calls, rollback/reopen and real HTTP. No password/OIDC login, browser cookie/BFF/CSRF implementation, email, object storage, RLS deployment or production security/load claim.

label: S12
title: Multi-tenant RAG knowledge-base platform
scope: Local RAG orchestration using unchanged S11 session/membership authority, versioned plaintext and durable ingest, deterministic feature-hash vectors/exact scan, current permission-before-top-k, extractive model fixture, strict quote/citation/tool validation, integer character-budget reservation and uncertainty, deletion/redaction/tombstones, six competing calls, selected judged corpus, rollback/reopen and real HTTP. No real LLM/embedding/vector API, learned semantic retrieval, external tools, stream, object store, provider metering or production quality/performance claim.

label: S13
title: Analytics event pipeline and dashboard
scope: Local SQLite durable event batches, scoped immutable event identity, offset checkpoint/effect atomicity, event-time cohorts, explicit watermark/late policy, generation rebuild, subject erasure marker, four competing calls, fault rollback/reopen and actual aggregate HTTP. No Kafka/Beam cluster, automatic watermark estimation, browser chart, external spreadsheet connector, secure disk/backup erasure or production capacity claim.
